work: The Æneid of Virgil translated into English prose

items.name: the wooden horse
items.description: Huge horse of timber built by the Greeks, hiding armed men, dragged into Troy to its ruin.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Trojan Horse was a wooden horse said to have been used by the Greeks during the Trojan War to sneak into the city of Troy and win the war. The Trojan Horse is not mentioned in Homer's Iliad, with the poem ending before the war is concluded, and it is only briefly mentioned in the Odyssey.

items.name: the golden bough
items.description: Golden branch found in the forest, offered to Proserpine, giving Æneas passage through the underworld.

wikipedia.lead: The Golden Bough is a fantastical object described in the Aeneid, an epic poem by the Roman poet Virgil composed between 29 and 19 BC narrating the adventures of the Trojan hero Aeneas after the Trojan War. The episode of the Golden Bough is found in its sixth book and is part of Aeneas's journey into the Underworld.

items.name: the shield of Æneas
items.description: Shield forged by Vulcan, showing the future history of Rome from Romulus to Actium and Augustus.

wikipedia.lead: The Shield of Aeneas is the shield that Aeneas receives from the god Vulcan in Book VIII of Virgil's Aeneid to aid in his war against the Rutuli. Imprinted on the front of the shield is a grand depiction of the destiny of Aeneas' descendants and the future of Rome.

items.name: the Palladium
items.description: Sacred image of Pallas guarding Troy, stolen by the Greeks, as Sinon's false tale recounts.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, the Palladium or Palladion was a cult image of great antiquity on which the safety of Troy and later Rome was said to depend, the wooden statue (xoanon) of Pallas Athena that Odysseus and Diomedes stole from the citadel of Troy and which was later taken to the future site of Rome by Aeneas. The Roman story is related in Virgil's Aeneid and other works.

items.name: Pallas' belt
items.description: Belt taken by Turnus from slain Pallas; seeing it, Æneas kills Turnus.

items.name: the Ægis
items.description: Divine shield-like emblem of the gods, borne by Pallas, bristling with serpents and the Gorgon's head.

wikipedia.lead: The aegis or egis, as stated in the Iliad, is a device carried by Zeus, Apollo and Athena, variously interpreted as an animal skin or a shield and sometimes featuring the head of a Gorgon. There may be a connection with a deity named Aex, a daughter of Helios and a nurse of Zeus or alternatively a mistress of Zeus (Hyginus, Astronomica 2.
